newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Ceara plans Coelce sale on May 6.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Ceara plans Coelce sale on May 6.

text.p: The Brazilian state of Ceara plans to auction off a 15-percent stake in its power distributor Coelce on May 6, a top company official said.
"The auction is scheduled for May 6 at the regional bourse of Fortaleza," said Coelce's financial director Oliver Sampaio.
The government plans to sell Coelce's 22.2 billion preferred shares, accounting for 41 percent of the firm's non-voting stakes, he said.
Sampaio denied market rumours that the company was planning to launch Level One American Depositary Receipts (ADRs).
He said Coelce has proposed its stockholders to make a share subscription amounting 50 million reais to pay for part of its 88 million reais investment plant this year.
However, nothing has been decided yet, he added.
"This proposal has not yet been approved by the state government," said Sampaio, noting that a share subscription now could undermine the upcoming sale of a minority stake in the firm.
Currently, Ceara state holds 89.5 percent of Coelce's voting or common stock and 71.4 percent of the firm's total capital.

Coelce, the third largest state-owned power utility in northeastern Brazil, has 1.3 million clients. Its sales last year totalled 475 million reais ($447.8 million), an increase of 8.9 percent over 1995.
This will be the first step towards the privatization of the company, which is expected to take place in 1998's first quarter, he said.
